Repair: sandbox.metering.DiskMemo - the deterministic memo's anchors are shared by every process of the machine (SQLite, first writer wins; the 3x + 1 ms tolerance rule and per-lineage keys unchanged); SandboxConfig.memo_path; worlds use metering.default_memo_path() ($CRUCIBLE_METER_MEMO, 'off' = per process; params.meter_memo='process' opts out). tests/test_v5_substrate_memo.py.

K2 tests failed after the merge: a world with an extra (observer) module or typed_events has another spec hash, hence another measurement lineage, and billed its sandboxed requests by fresh measurements. params.meter_lineage lets an experiment's arms share a lineage; the K2 tests give every arm the same lineage, and a new test shows that without it only ext/cloud.usage events differ (the measurement confound).

Cross-process determinism of sandboxed work holds on one machine given the machine-level memo (first measurement wins); a fresh machine measures afresh, and a computation measured above 3x its anchor + 1 ms is billed fresh (honest, nondeterministic). social/studio.py's own sandbox pool and rapid/engines/program_exec.py use the deterministic cost model with meter_scope None and no memo file: anchors shared by all worlds of a process, not across processes (owners C and H).

Snapshot bytes grow superlinearly (each snapshot holds the state, which keeps one artifacts metadata row per system blob: 222,702 rows after 365 days; 15 retained snapshots = 120 MB at day 365, growing 1.4 -> 3.3 MB/week). Blob and event growth rates are constant.

Historical runtime reconstruction (history.state_at(..., runtime=True)) is available only at times whose neural checkpoints are still stored: collect drops superseded checkpoints that no retained snapshot roots. State queries (runtime=False) stay exact at any time.

Wall time per simulated day grew 2.45 -> 4.49 s over 365 days; the weekly compaction was the main O(history) term (19.3 s at day 365); after the incremental fix a warm weekly compaction at day 372-379 takes 8.8-9.4 s (packing that week's blobs included), the remaining O(blobs) part being two blob-size scans (1.8 s); a full 365-day run was not repeated after the fix.
Fault injection still reaches few agent commands (random schema-valid commands rarely span modules); deliberate composed failures come from a labelled test driver module.
Cross-process exactness is verified on this machine (CPU torch), not across machines.
The event log is not bounded (linear, as any exact record); SQLite stores payloads > 2 KiB compressed, Postgres (JSON columns) does not.

Main-line isolation covers same-transaction subscribers. Couplings implemented as scheduled processes, or sharing kernel counters (unkeyed sched job ids), still shift later main-line positions; appliers that store an event's absolute seq in state (4.0 search_docs.seq) differ in that field when side events exist.

Bytes uploaded through the artifact.put tool are also in the recorded cmd event (arguments are recorded for regeneration); module code should store large media with artifacts.put, whose events hold only the REF.
A world moved to another store must run artifacts.export(world, dest_store) before it is loaded in another process.
